title: Your temporary files
explanation: Programs and installers leave temporary files here and often forget them. Only items untouched for 2+ days are included, and anything in use is skipped.

title: Windows temporary files
explanation: Temporary files from Windows Update, installers and services. Only items untouched for 2+ days are included.

title: Graphics shader cache
explanation: Pre-compiled shaders for games. It refills while you play (the first launch of a game may stutter briefly), and caches of games you no longer have are never cleaned up automatically.

title: Graphics driver installer files
explanation: Extracted driver installers. The installed driver doesn't need them.

title: Crash dumps
explanation: Memory snapshots saved when programs crashed. Only developers use them.

title: Windows crash dumps
explanation: Saved after blue screens and driver hangs. Only useful if you are troubleshooting those right now.

title: Full memory dump
explanation: Written after a blue screen. Often several gigabytes and only useful for debugging that crash.

title: Windows error reports
explanation: Problem reports that Windows already sent (or gave up sending) to Microsoft.

title: Windows Update download cache
explanation: Update files that have already been installed. Don't clean it while an update is installing; Windows re-downloads anything it still needs.

title: Internet cache (Windows)
explanation: Web content cached by Windows components and older apps.

title: Browser cache
explanation: Copies of websites the browser keeps to load pages faster. Logins, history and bookmarks are not touched. Close the browser first for the best result.

title: App cache
explanation: Downloaded images, songs and web content an app keeps for speed. The app downloads what it needs again.

title: Epic Games Launcher cache
explanation: Downloaded store content, web pages and installer leftovers of the Epic Games Launcher.

title: Developer package cache
explanation: Packages downloaded by programming tools. They are fetched again on your next build or install, which takes time and internet.

title: Hibernation file
explanation: Holds your memory while the PC hibernates; Fast Startup uses it too.
advice: If you never use hibernation, turn it off in an administrator terminal. That removes this file and disables Fast Startup (startups get a little slower).

title: Page file (virtual memory)
explanation: Extra memory on disk that Windows uses when RAM fills up.
advice: Leave it to Windows unless you know you need a change: System Properties > Advanced > Performance Settings > Advanced > Virtual memory.

title: Previous Windows installation
explanation: Kept after a Windows upgrade so you can go back. Windows removes it on its own after about 10 days.
advice: Remove it through Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > Previous Windows installation(s).

title: Windows component store (WinSxS)
explanation: Copies of Windows parts kept for updates and repairs. It looks bigger than it is, because many files are also counted under System32.
advice: Let Windows clean out superseded versions with DISM in an administrator terminal.

title: Windows Installer cache
explanation: Patches and installers that programs need in order to update, repair or uninstall.
advice: Don't delete these by hand: programs would become impossible to update or uninstall. Uninstalling programs you no longer use is what shrinks it.

title: System Restore points
explanation: Snapshots that let you roll Windows back after a bad update or driver.
advice: Cap or clear them in System Protection: select the drive > Configure > lower Max Usage, or Delete.

title: Delivery Optimization files
explanation: Update pieces Windows shares with other PCs.
advice: Clear them in Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > Delivery Optimization Files.
